Zimbabwe captain Josephine Nkomo has won the toss and opted to field first against Pakistan at the Seven Districts Ground, Ajman on Monday. Pakistan are placed second in Group B with two wins and one loss, while Zimbabwe are placed third in the table.  Koushik Paul Updated 16 Nov 2026, 11:43 AM IST Prefer Livemint on Google Zimbabwe captain Josephine Nkomo (L) has won the toss and opted to field first against Pakistan. ( PCB ) AI Quick Read A day after being stunned by lower-ranked Netherlands, the Pakistan women's cricket team would be aiming to bounce back in the ongoing 2026 Women's Emerging Nations Trophy against Zimbabwe at the Seven Districts Ground, Ajman on Monday. This is the last group-stage match for Pakistan before the Super Six stage. Having won against Bangladesh and Thailand in their first two Group B encounters, Pakistan women have four points from three games and sit second in the table behind table-toppers Netherlands. With Zimbabwe having played a match less, a win against Zimbabwe will further consolidate Pakistan's position in the group among the top three. Also Read | India vs Pakistan Women’s Asia Cup 2026: 5 players who could decide the clash The top three teams from both the groups will advance into the Super Six stage, from where the top four qualify for the semifinals. Pakistan women vs Zimbabwe women toss report Zimbabwe captain Josephine Nkomo has won the toss and opted to field first against Pakistan. Led by Muneeba Ali, Pakistan have made one change, replacing Waheeda Akhtar, with left-arm pacer Tasmia Rubab. On the other hand, Zimbabwe are playing with an unchanged side. Where to watch PAK-W vs ZIM-W in India? No television channel has bought the broadcast rights for the ICC Women's Emerging Nations Trophy 2026 in India. However, fans can still watch the live streaming of Pakistan women vs Zimbabwe women and all other matches on FanCode app and website. After transitioning from his own aspirations of becoming a professional athlete, he successfully channeled that lifelong passion into a prolific career, documenting the action both from the sidelines and the editorial desk. With over eight years of industry experience, Koushik joined LiveMint as a Deputy Chief Content Producer in 2024, following impactful stints at Outlook India, India.com, Sportskeeda, Women’s CricZone, and OrissaPOST. A 2017 Journalism and Mass Communication graduate from Maharaja Manindra Chandra College, Kolkata, Koushik has reported on high-profile events including the FIFA U17 World Cup 2017, Ranji Trophy, FIH Pro League, FIH World League finals, the Indian Premier League, and Lionel Messi’s historic visit to Kolkata in 2025.

While he possesses a versatile command over all sports, he finds his niche in cricket, specializing in breaking news, long-form interviews, global sporting updates, and high-energy live blogs. Koushik’s professional perspective was further sharpened through the 2020 AIPS Young Reporters Programme, where he gained invaluable insights from renowned international journalists, including Keir Radnedge and Riccardo Romani from the United Kingdom, and Martin Mazur from Argentina. Currently based between Kolkata and Delhi, Koushik remains at the forefront of the breaking developments that shape the public sporting discourse. When he isn't tracking scores or deconstructing plays, he can be found exploring new landscapes on his travels or channeling his creative energy into the kitchen.
